evidence.excerpt: Two modelling strategies for predicting conducted emissions from LED retrofit lamp drivers are compared: a behavioural model based on measured Thevenin equivalent source impedance and voltage, and a circuit-level model derived from the reverse-engineered schematic of three driver types with rated power of 7 W, 12 W and 18 W. Both models are embedded in a low-voltage network simulation and evaluated against LISN measurements over 150 kHz to 30 MHz. The behavioural approach reproduces measured emission profiles with an average RMS error of 3.1 dB but requires individual characterisation of each unit. The circuit-level model achieves 4.7 dB average error without unit-specific measurement but is sensitive to uncertainty in parasitic component values. A hybrid procedure combining measured impedance data with a simplified circuit skeleton reduces average error to 2.6 dB. The study covers 15 driver samples from four unnamed market sources. Implications for aggregated emission prediction when large numbers of LED luminaires are installed on a single feeder are discussed, with a Monte Carlo analysis of 50 to 500 simultaneous loads.
